rv.q: The drop-dead funny national tour of Beetlejuice, now playing at Broadway San Jose, is a grave delight.
Brash, ribald, frequently raw and shamelessly sappy and containing a witty score by Eddie Perfect, it’s pretty damned irresistible.
Fans of the film will enjoy the nostalgia and appreciate how naturally its theatricality translates to the stage, while newcomers can surrender to this very specific world.
Its greatest trick isn't raising the dead, it's resurrecting the unabashed enthusiasm that first draws people into musical theatre.
Death is an unlikely subject for a feel-good musical, but this show pulls it off.
All of the actors certainly tried their best to exude energy and charisma, but it was difficult to sustain interest in such a loud and garish stage environment.
In this case, Beetlejuice makes death a whole lot of fun.
That contrast of absurd comedy paired with real emotion is what gave the production staying power.
Ryan Stajmiger's Beetlejuice is everything this character should be. Hilarious, menacing, maniacal and, above all, entertaining.
It’s packed with slapstick, quick-witted humor and over-the-top performances that will leave audiences smiling all night.
It's a raucous, profane, and very funny show with some real standout songs with actual emotional heft.
Now back at the National on its second national tour stop here since 2023, the show still seems stuck in limbo.

cn.t: Critics find this energetic screen-to-stage adaptation a visually dazzling spectacle with strong laughs, though some question its substance. Ryan Stajmiger's chaotic title performance and Eddie Perfect's songs win praise from most reviewers.
